SMTO-FIL-0020 — SMTO's file changes didn't match the files as they are now

GUID: f1879da7-b9a7-44ed-aa62-7e20feb7ce11
Slug: file-patch-conflict
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO prepared changes to one or more files, but they were badly formed or no longer line up with what the files contain now. None of these changes were applied.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to read the files again and redo its changes based on what they contain now. The changes were lined up against an older version of the files.
  2. If someone else is editing the same files, wait until they finish or close the other program, then ask SMTO to try again. Edits made at the same time move the lines SMTO's changes depend on.
  3. If SMTO is changing many files at once, ask it to change them one at a time. Smaller sets of changes are less likely to be malformed and are easier to check.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the changes as applied and each file shows the new content.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to overwrite the files with its own copy to force the changes in; that can erase newer work.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file.patch was rejected during preflight because the unified diff is malformed (bad header or quoted path, hunk counts not matching the body, overlapping or out-of-range hunks, duplicate targets) or its context lines do not exactly match current file content; no file was written.

What this means

  • Patch parsing, hunk counts/order, duplicate paths or exact current-content matching failed. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Patch parsing, hunk counts/order, duplicate paths or exact current-content matching failed.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish invalid patch format from revision/context conflict by inspecting safe parser/hunk diagnostics.

How to fix it

  • Regenerate the unified diff from freshly read content with exact context lines and correct @@ counts, one header per target, and pass current expected_revisions; the receipt message names the parser or hunk rule that failed (gateway_core/file_patch.parse_patch, apply_hunks, patch).
  • Correct the patch format or regenerate its hunks against current content before applying it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid patch matches the reviewed current files and passes preflight.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
